# I. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for type (combined) with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_beta_type <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: NONE.  Howvever, add centre as improves regularisation.


## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_type <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ type
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_type,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_type)
```

```{r}

```


## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_type) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```





### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_type_prior_only <- update(mod_type, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_type_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```








### 3. Check posterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_type)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_type_prior_only)
```



#### b. type_ab
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "typeab"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior vs posterior for  type AB", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of type AB", xlim = c(-1, 3),  ylim = c(0, 1.4)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "typeab"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```





##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "typeab"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "typeab"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "typeab"] - mean(prior_draws[, "typeab"])))

```






#### b. type_b
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
```{r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "typeb"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior vs posterior for type B", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of type B", xlim = c(-2, 3), ylim = c(0, 1.4)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "typeb"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "typeb"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "typeb"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "typeb"] - mean(prior_draws[, "typeb"])))

```



### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for type variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = FALSE),
  main = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```



#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ type 
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
##### i. type_ab
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio for type_ab across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(typeab, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio for type_ab across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "typeab", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```







##### ii. type_b
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio for type_ab across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(typeb, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio for type_ab across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "typeb", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```



Text for paper:
"Prior–likelihood compatibility was assessed using prior predictive checks and by comparing prior and posterior marginal distributions of key parameters. Sensitivity analyses were performed by refitting models under weaker and stronger priors; substantive conclusions were robust to these choices.”





## Make model predictions and plot
### 1. Create new data where type differs
```{r}
nd1 <- data.frame(type = c("a", "b", "ab"),
                 centre = c("p", "p", "p"))
head(nd1)
```




#### 2. Make posterior predictions from new data
```{r}
ps <- posterior_survfit(mod_type,
  newdata = nd1,
  times = 0,
  extrapolate = TRUE) |>
  suppressWarnings()
head(ps)
```




#### 3. Plot
```{r}
panel_labels <- c('1' = "Type A", '2' = "Type B", '3' = "Type AB")
pps <- plot(ps) +
  aes(colour = factor(id), fill = factor(id)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels)) +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 10),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 10)) +
            theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold.italic"),
                    strip.background = element_rect(fill="white") ) +
            scale_colour_hue(h.start = 120) +
            scale_fill_hue(h.start = 120)
        
print(pps)
```

#### create plots

## Create KM curve
```{r}


# Basic KM curve for the entire dataset
km_strat <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + type, data = df)

# Convert to tidy format
km_df <- broom::tidy(km_strat)
km_df$strata2 <- ifelse(grepl("type=b", km_df$strata), "Type B",
                       ifelse(grepl("type=ab", km_df$strata), "Type AB", "Type A"))

km_df$strata2 <- factor(km_df$strata2, levels = c("Type A", "Type B", "Type AB"))

# Columns: time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, strata, n.risk, n.event, n.censor
ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = strata2, fill = strata2)) +
  geom_step() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "Stenosis type",
    fill = "Stenosis type",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by stenosis type"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=16, face="bold"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 14),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 14),
               legend.title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               legend.position = c(0.87, 0.88),
               legend.text = element_text(size=12)) +
            scale_colour_hue(h.start = 120) +
            scale_fill_hue(h.start = 120)
            
```

```{r}
  data = df)

summary(freq_cox_type)
```

# II. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for s_age with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_age <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: NONE.  However, add centre as improves regularisation.




## Fit model with for s_age
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_age <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_age
                     + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_age,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```




## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_age)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_age)
```



## Check model performance
### 1.Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_age) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_age_prior_only <- update(mod_age, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_age_prior_only)  |>
  suppressWarnings()
```





### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_age)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_age_prior_only)
```



#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_age"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior vs posterior for age", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of age", xlim = c(-1, 1) ) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_age"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```


#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_age"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_age"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_age"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_age"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_age variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```



#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_age
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for age across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_age, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_age", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# III.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for EFFECT OF SURGERY (surgery y/n) with random intercept for centre


## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_beta_sx <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE))
```
NB needed to set a tighter scale variable for prior_intercept and also prior_beta_sx in order to improve regularisation and resolve divergent transitions.

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: age, clin signs, concurrent congen, pressure grad, referral centre, stenosis type.




## Fit model with for surgery (plus correction set)
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_sx <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ surgery
                    + s_age
                    + concurrent_congenital
                    + type
                    + clinical_signs
                    + s_pv_max_pg

  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_sx,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

# IV.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of RV SYSTOLIC DYSFUNCTION (tapse) with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_rdys <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: pressure grad, referral centre, stenosis type.



## Fit model with for s_tapse
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}

mod_rsdys <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_tapse
                       + s_pv_max_pg
                       + type
                       + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_rdys,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2.5, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

```{r}
prior_summary(mod_rsdys)
```

## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}

  suppressWarnings()
```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_rsdys_prior_only <- update(mod_rsdys, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_rsdys_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```








### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_rsdys)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_rsdys_prior_only)
```




#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_tapse"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior v posterior for TAPSE", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of TAPSE", xlim = c(-1.5, 0.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_tapse"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```




#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_tapse"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_tapse"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_tapse"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_tapse"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_tapse variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))
)
```



#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_tapse
                       + s_pv_max_pg
                       + type
                       + (1| centre),
            data = df,
            basehaz = "ms",
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_tapse, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_tapse", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```




#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_pv_max_pg"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_pv_max_pg variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_pv_max_pg
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_pv_max_pg, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_pv_max_pg", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# VI.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of NFD (s_vtiao_vtipv) with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_nfd <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = TRUE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: pressure grad, referral centre.





## Fit model with for s_vtiao_vtipv

```{r}
  prior = prior_beta_nfd,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

``` {r}
dens(post_draws[, "s_vmaxav_vmaxpv"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for Ao Vmax / P Vmax", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of Vmax AV : Vmax PV", xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(0, 3))
```

#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean

```{r}
mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_vmaxav_vmaxpv"] - beta_hat) <

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_vmaxav_vmaxpv
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_vmaxav_vmaxpv, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_vmaxav_vmaxpv", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

## Create KM curve
```{r}


# Basic KM curve for the entire dataset
km_strat <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + vmaxav_vmaxpv_quartile, data = df)

# Convert to tidy format and reorder strata for plotting
km_df <- broom::tidy(km_strat)
km_df$strata2 <- ifelse(grepl("vmaxav_vmaxpv_quartile=Q1", km_df$strata), "Quartile 1",
                          ifelse(grepl("vmaxav_vmaxpv_quartile=Q2", km_df$strata), "Quartile 2",
                                 ifelse(grepl("vmaxav_vmaxpv_quartile=Q3", km_df$strata), "Quartile 3",
                                        ifelse(grepl("vmaxav_vmaxpv_quartile=Q4", km_df$strata), "Quartile 4", NA))))

# Columns: time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, strata, n.risk, n.event, n.censor
ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = strata2, fill = strata2)) +
  geom_step() +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "Vmax AV : Vmax PV",
    fill = "Vmax AV : Vmax PV",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by Vmax AV : Vmax PV quartile"
    ) +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=16, face="bold"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 14),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 14),
               legend.title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               legend.position = c(0.84, 0.85),
               legend.text = element_text(size=13)
            )
```

# VIII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of RV HYPERTROPHY (s_ed_rvfw) with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_rvhyp <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment set: NFD values, referral centre, stenosis type.



## Fit model with for s_ed_rvfw (plus correction set)
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_rvhyp <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_ed_rvfw
                       + s_vmaxav_vmaxpv
                       + type
                       + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_rvhyp,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

```{r}
km_strat <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + ed_rvfw_quartile, data = df)

# Convert to tidy format and reorder strata for plotting
km_df <- broom::tidy(km_strat)
km_df$strata2 <- ifelse(grepl("ed_rvfw_quartile=Q1", km_df$strata), "Quartile 1",
                          ifelse(grepl("ed_rvfw_quartile=Q2", km_df$strata), "Quartile 2",
                                 ifelse(grepl("ed_rvfw_quartile=Q3", km_df$strata), "Quartile 3",
                                        ifelse(grepl("ed_rvfw_quartile=Q4", km_df$strata), "Quartile 4", NA))))

# Columns: time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, strata, n.risk, n.event, n.censor
ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = strata2, fill = strata2)) +
  geom_step() +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "ED RVFW",
    fill = "ED RVFW",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by ED RVFW quartile"
    ) +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=16, face="bold"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 14),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 14),
               legend.title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               legend.position = c(0.85, 0.85),
               legend.text = element_text(size=13)
            )
```

### 2. Check performance of prior probability

```{r}
mod_radil_prior_only <- update(mod_radil, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_radil_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_radil)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_radil_prior_only)
```




#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for RA max diameter", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of RA max diameter", xlim = c(-0.5, 1.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```




#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 0.5, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_ra_max_diam
                       + s_vmaxav_vmaxpv
                       + s_pv_max_pg
                       + s_ed_rvfw
                       + concurrent_congenital
                       + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```




#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_ra_max_diam, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_ra_max_diam", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```






#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "chf1"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "chf1"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "chf1"] - mean(prior_draws[, "chf1"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 0.5, autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ chf
                     + concurrent_congenital
                     + type
                     + s_tapse
                     + s_pv_max_pg
                     + arrhythmias
                     + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(chf1, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "chf1", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```


### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 01, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ atenolol_pre
                      + s_tapse
                      + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(atenolol_pre, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "atenolol_pre", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XIIb.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of ATENOLOL post with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_aten_post <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 3, autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: RV syst dys, aten pre, referral centre (and sx yes).
NB need to use surgery df to ensure that the analysis is only on dogs that have had surgery.



## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_aten_post <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ atenolol_post
                      + s_tapse
                      + atenolol_pre
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df_surg,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_aten_post,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
  init = 0.1,
  seed = 666)
```

# XIII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of PROCEDURE TYPE with SEPARATE VARIABLES (balloon / stent) random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_prtyp <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: concurrent congen, referral centre, stenosis type (and sx yes).
NB need to use surgery df to ensure that the analysis is only on dogs that have had surgery.




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_prtyp <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ balloon * stent
                        + concurrent_congenital
                        + type
                        + (1| centre),
  data = df_surg,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_prtyp,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior

#### b. Balloon
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "balloon"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for balloon valvulopasty", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of balloon valvuloplasty", xlim = c(-5, 5), ylim = c(0, 0.35)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "balloon"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "balloon"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "balloon"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "balloon"] - mean(prior_draws[, "balloon"])))

```

### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ balloon * stent
                        + concurrent_congenital
                        + type_a
                        + (1| centre),,
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios cross different priors
##### i. balloon
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(balloon, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "balloon", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```




##### ii. stent

## Create KM curve
```{r}
# Basic KM curve for the entire dataset
km_strat <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + proc_type, data = df_surg)

# Convert to tidy format and reorder strata for plotting
km_df <- broom::tidy(km_strat)
km_df$strata2 <- ifelse(grepl("proc_type=balloon", km_df$strata), "Balloon",
                       ifelse(grepl("proc_type=stent", km_df$strata), "Stent", "Balloon and stent"))
km_df$strata2 <- factor(km_df$strata2, levels = c("Balloon", "Stent", "Balloon and stent"))

# Columns: time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, strata, n.risk, n.event, n.censor
ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = strata2, fill = strata2)) +
  geom_step() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "Procedure type",
    fill = "Procedure type",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by procedure type"
    ) +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=16, face="bold"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 14),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 14),
               legend.title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               legend.position = c(0.83, 0.15),
               legend.text = element_text(size=12)
            )
```

# XIVa.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of COMPLICATIONS with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_comp <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: high pressure, low pressure, referral centre, stent.
NB need to include balloon type here as well for an appropriate adjustment set


## Need to create separate variables for high pressure and low pressure so as to model complications appropriately
```{r}
df_surg$high_pressure <- ifelse(df_surg$balloon_type == "high_pressure", 1, 0)
df_surg$high_pressure[is.na(df_surg$high_pressure)] <- 0
df_surg$low_pressure <- ifelse(df_surg$balloon_type == "low_pressure", 1, 0)
df_surg$low_pressure[is.na(df_surg$low_pressure)] <- 0
```




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_comp <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ complications
                      + stent
                      + high_pressure
                      + low_pressure
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df_surg,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_comp,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_comp)
```

```{r}

```



### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_comp)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_comp_prior_only)
```



#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "complications1"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for complications", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of complications", xlim = c(-3, 3)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "complications1"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "complications1"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "complications1"] - mean(prior_draws[, "complications1"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ complications
                      + stent
                      + high_pressure
                      + low_pressure
                      + (1| centre),
            data = df_surg,
            basehaz = "ms",
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(complications1, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "complications1", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

```{r}

  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "Complication",
    fill = "Complication",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by complication after intervention"
    ) +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"),

               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=16, face="bold"),
```

# XIVb.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of COMPLICATIONS_2 with random intercept for centre and control set
This model excludes dogs that died during the surgical procedure

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_comp2 <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: high pressure, low pressure, referral centre, stent.
NB need to include balloon type here as well for an appropriate adjustment set


## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_comp2 <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ complications_2
                      + stent
                      + high_pressure
                      + low_pressure
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df_surg,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_comp2,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```


# XV.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of CONCURRENT CONGENITAL with random intercept for centre
No control set required for the causal effect to be estimated.

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)

```{r}
prior_beta_cong <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_cong <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ concurrent_congenital
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_cong,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

``` {r}
dens(post_draws[, "concurrent_congenital1"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for concurrent congenital disease", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of concurrent congenital disease", xlim = c(-0.5, 2.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "concurrent_congenital1"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean

### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for concurrent congenital variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ concurrent_congenital
                      + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(concurrent_congenital1, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "concurrent_congenital1", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XVI.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of CLINICAL SIGNS with random intercept for centre
No control set required for the causal effect to be estimated.


## Neutral prior for clinicial signs
No prior information on the effect of clinical signs
Therefore, set a Neutral weekly regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_clin_si <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: Right CHF, arrhyth.  However, also add centre as improves regularisation.



## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_clin_si <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ clinical_signs
                         + chf
                         + arrhythmias
                         + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_clin_si,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

# XVII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of BALLOON TYPE with random intercept for centre
Have conditioned on balloon use... by using the df_balloon dataset which only includes dogs that had a balloon procedure.  This conditions on surgery (only including those that had a procedure, and then use of balloon in procedure_type) Therefore, no control set required (other than including centre as a grouping variable) for the causal effect to be estimated.

## Neutral prior for clinicial signs
No prior information on the effect of clinical signs
Therefore, set a Neutral weekly regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_balloon_type <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: proc type, referral centre, stenosis type.
NB to include procedure type, simply use df_balloon as that will ensure anaylsis only includes dogs that had a balloon procedure.



## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_balloon_type <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ balloon_type
```

``` {r}
dens(prior_draws[, "balloon_typehigh_pressure"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean

```{r}

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for balloon type variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ balloon_type
                              + type
                              + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df_balloon,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(balloon_typehigh_pressure, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "balloon_typehigh_pressure", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

## Create KM curve
```{r}


# Basic KM curve for the entire dataset
km_strat <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + balloon_type, data = df_balloon)

# Convert to tidy format and reorder strata for plotting
km_df <- broom::tidy(km_strat)
km_df$strata2 <- ifelse(grepl("balloon_type=low_pressure", km_df$strata), "Low pressure", "High pressure")
km_df$strata2 <- factor(km_df$strata2, levels = c("Low pressure", "High pressure"))

# Columns: time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, strata, n.risk, n.event, n.censor
ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = strata2, fill = strata2)) +
  geom_step() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "Balloon type",
    fill = "Balloon type",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by balloon type"
    ) +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=16, face="bold"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 14),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 14),
               legend.title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               legend.position = c(0.87, 0.85),
               legend.text = element_text(size=13)
            )
```

```{r}
summary(freq_cox_balloon_type)
```

# XVIII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of RV SYSTOLIC DYSFUNCTION (normalised TAPSE: tapse_n) with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_rdysn <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: pressure grad, referral centre, stenosis type.



## Fit model with for s_tapse_n
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}

mod_rsdysn <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_tapse_n
                       + s_pv_max_pg
                       + type
                       + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_rdysn,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2.5, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

```{r}
                                 ifelse(grepl("tapse_n_quartile=Q3", km_df$strata), "Quartile 3",
                                        ifelse(grepl("tapse_n_quartile=Q4", km_df$strata), "Quartile 4", NA))))

# Columns: time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, strata, n.risk, n.event, n.censor
ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = strata2, fill = strata2)) +
  geom_step() +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "TAPSE",
    fill = "TAPSE",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by TAPSE quartile"
    ) +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=16, face="bold"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 14),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 14),
               legend.title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               legend.position = c(0.87, 0.15),
               legend.text = element_text(size=13)
            )
```

# XIX.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of RV HYPERTROPHY (normalised ED RVFW: s_ed_rvfw_n) with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_rvhypn <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment set: NFD values, referral centre, stenosis type.



## Fit model with for s_ed_rvfw_n (plus correction set)
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_rvhypn <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_ed_rvfw_n
                       + s_vmaxav_vmaxpv
                       + type
                       + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_rvhypn,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 10000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

```{r}

```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_rvhypn_prior_only <- update(mod_rvhypn, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_rvhypn_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_rvhypn)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_rvhypn_prior_only)
```



#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for RVFWd", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of RVFWd", xlim = c(-0.5, 1.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_ed_rvfw_n
                       + s_vmaxav_vmaxpv
                       + type
                       + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_ed_rvfw_n, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_ed_rvfw_n", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam_n"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for RAD", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of RAD", xlim = c(-0.5, 1.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam_n"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam_n"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam_n"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam_n"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_ra_max_diam_n"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 0.5, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_ra_max_diam_n
                       + s_vmaxav_vmaxpv
                       + s_pv_max_pg
                       + s_ed_rvfw
                       + concurrent_congenital
                       + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_ab across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_ra_max_diam_n, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_ra_max_diam_n", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

## Create KM curve
```{r}


# Basic KM curve for the entire dataset
km_strat <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1 + ra_max_diam_n_quartile, data = df)

# Convert to tidy format and reorder strata for plotting
km_df <- broom::tidy(km_strat)
km_df$strata2 <- ifelse(grepl("ra_max_diam_n_quartile=Q1", km_df$strata), "Quartile 1",
                          ifelse(grepl("ra_max_diam_n_quartile=Q2", km_df$strata), "Quartile 2",
                                 ifelse(grepl("ra_max_diam_n_quartile=Q3", km_df$strata), "Quartile 3",
                                        ifelse(grepl("ra_max_diam_n_quartile=Q4", km_df$strata), "Quartile 4", NA))))

# Columns: time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, strata, n.risk, n.event, n.censor
ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = strata2, fill = strata2)) +
  geom_step() +
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Survival probability",
    colour = "RA max diameter",
    fill = "RA max diameter",
    title = "Kaplan–Meier curves stratified by RA max diameter quartile"
    ) +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=16, face="bold"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 14),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 14),
               legend.title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               legend.position = c(0.85, 0.15),
               legend.text = element_text(size=13)
            )
```
